meta.title: WorkBuddy browser
meta.description: Drives your own already-logged-in Chrome or Edge tabs through the WorkBuddy browser extension: click buttons and links, fill in forms, scroll and page through results, take screenshots, read dynamically rendered content, and walk multi-step web workflows. Use it when a page needs real login state or real interaction rather than a plain HTTP fetch. It requires WorkBuddy running, the WorkBuddy extension installed and enabled in the browser you want to drive, and at least one open tab — the install entry point is WorkBuddy's Settings › Agent › Browser control, using the Install button beside each browser; the numbered steps are on the bundle's detail page. Tools are named mcp__workbuddy__*; call mcp__workbuddy__browsers_list first for a browser_id. Tools missing means WorkBuddy or the extension is not reachable; tools present but an empty browser list means the extension is not installed, not enabled, or no tab is open. Cost and risk: this acts on your live session, and both tabs_finalize and tabs_close close tabs — tabs_finalize closes them even when marked handoff on some browsers, so never use it to tidy up; to keep a page do nothing, and call tabs_close only on tabs the agent opened with tabs_new; tabs taken over with tabs_claim are yours and must never be passed to tabs_finalize. Heavily client-rendered pages such as iWiki sometimes return an empty visible-DOM snapshot; fall back to tab_screenshot with coordinate actions there. Turning this plugin off removes those tools; nothing else in the harness changes.
